subject: SLA carveout and quota uplift for Sep 19 weekend trading run
messages:
From: Alan Cho <alan.cho@quantifytrade.com>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.inference>
Cc: procurement@quantifytrade.com
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2026 09:14:00 -0400
Subject: Request: weekend quota uplift for Sep 19 trading run

Hi Dylan,

We have a scheduled end-of-day reconciliation for an options bucket on Sep 19 (Saturday) that will generate a concentrated spike of inference traffic for about 6 hours (00:00–06:00 UTC). We estimate peak QPS per endpoint around 380–420 and an aggregate token throughput increase of ~4.5x vs normal weekend baselines. I attached a quick CSV with the per-endpoint estimates.

Two asks: can Redwood support a temporary quota uplift for that window without being throttled by fairness policies, and are there any SLA implications we should be aware of (latency commitments under this uplift)? We want to avoid missing deadlines for downstream settlement jobs.

We can provide a PO/amendment if needed. Please advise what information you need from our side (endpoint patterns, auth keys to pre-warm caches, etc.).

Thanks,
Alan Cho
Head of Platform
QuantifyTrade

Attachments: expected-traffic.csv (CSV)
From: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.inference>
To: Alan Cho <alan.cho@quantifytrade.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>, rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: weekend quota uplift for Sep 19 trading run

Alan — thanks for the details and the CSV. We can support a temporary uplift for the 6-hour window, but I want to confirm a few things so we scope the right path (hosted vs dedicated burst) and preserve our fairness policy for other customers.

Quick answers up front:
- Short yes: a time-limited quota uplift is possible.
- SLA impact: we can provide an elevated throughput window with a documented latency SLO for the duration, but it requires a signed amendment (DocuSign) and an internal carveout to the fairness/throttle policy for the specified window.

Can you confirm:
1) Which endpoints are involved (generation vs embeddings vs streaming)?
2) Exact UTC window you want us to cover (you mentioned 00:00–06:00 UTC on Sep 19) — are you okay with a 30-minute canary leading into the full window?
3) Billing contact and PO number for the amendment.

Proposed approach:
- We provision a temporary dedicated burst pool reserved for your traffic during the 6-hour window. Requests during the window will be routed to the reserved pool; if capacity is exceeded we will route to fallback model variants with degraded latency guarantees rather than drop traffic.
- We’ll carve out a fairness policy exemption tied to a single API key and time range, backed by the signed amendment. The carveout will include a hard cap to avoid unbounded use.
- Pre-warm: please provide the top 10 prompt patterns / authorization keys so we can pre-warm KV caches.

I’ve attached a one-page template (quantify_sla_request.xlsx) that captures the info we need to complete the amendment and technical runbook. Marissa — can you validate the capacity estimate and suggest exact uplift numbers? Karthik — can you confirm the operational risk and whether we need a temporary runbook for our operations team (pager override window, etc.)?

If everyone is aligned I’ll send the DocuSign amendment and a short runbook.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: quantify_sla_request.xlsx (XLSX)
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.inference>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>, rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2026 15:21:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: weekend quota uplift for Sep 19 trading run

Folks — reviewed the CSV and Dylan’s ask. Notes below (operational/tech):

Summary estimate:
- If peak QPS ~420, we recommend reserving a dedicated burst pool sized for ~500 QPS headroom (to account for burstiness).
- Disk-backed KV cache pre-warm of top 10 prefixes should reduce token re-computation; still budget for ~20% higher token cost on the first hour.

Fairness policy & risk:
- Carveouts are permitted when backed by a signed amendment + explicit time windows. We should limit the carveout to the specific API key(s) and the 00:00–06:00 UTC window.
- Recommend a 30-minute canary at 75% of uplifted QPS before we flip the full 100%. Can add a rule to auto-scale + throttle to fallback models if latency exceeds 350ms p50 for 2 consecutive minutes.

Operational runbook items:
- Pager override: ops on-call to treat the window as elevated priority (clear escalation path).
- Rolling rollback: if errors >1% for 5 consecutive minutes, flip traffic to fallback model and notify QuantifyTrade SRE.

Suggested uplift numbers (for amendment):
- Baseline quota: current limits (as in account config).
- Temporary uplift: +4x token quota, peak QPS cap = 500, burst token cap = 2.5M tokens per hour.

I attached a short capacity calc PDF. If we go dedicated, finance will need to sign off on the short-term commitment — Dylan, we’ll work with you on pricing.

-Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: capacity_calc.pdf (PDF)

Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2026 08:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: weekend quota uplift for Sep 19 trading run

Alan — thanks, Marissa’s team ran the numbers and we have an operational plan. Summary and next steps below.

Plan (high level):
1) Canary window: Sep 19 23:30–00:00 UTC (30 min) at 75% uplift.
2) Full uplift: Sep 19 00:00–06:00 UTC (6 hours) capped at 500 QPS and 2.5M tokens/hour.
3) Fairness carveout: tied to a single API key and the exact UTC window; auto-fallback to model variants if latency >350ms p50.
4) Ops: Pager override + rollback criteria as Marissa described.

Next steps for you:
- Please confirm endpoints and provide the top 10 prompt patterns (for pre-warm).
- Sign the attached amendment via DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/recipient/url?doc=QT-7831-amend (this link is a one-click route to the amendment).
- Confirm billing contact / PO number so finance can prepare the short-term dedicated estimate.

I’m copying procurement here. Once we have the signed amendment and the pre-warm patterns we’ll lock the reserved burst pool and send the final runbook.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 15-minute call if you want to walk through the runbook.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
